  Q: What Medicare coverage pathway for GLP-1s used for obesity was announced in
  late 2025, and when does it take effect?
  Tier 3 · split train · glp1 · coverage_pathway

  Draft summary: In November 2025 the administration announced pricing
  agreements with Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly. They included a Medicare coverage
  pathway for GLP-1s for some beneficiaries with obesity, with BMI and
  comorbidity criteria and a fixed copay. In December 2025 CMS announced an
  Innovation Center model for GLP-1 coverage in Medicaid and Part D. The answer
  must give the effective dates and current status from primary CMS/HHS sources.

  Required claims
  - c1 (must): a Nov 2025 pricing agreement with Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly
    included a Medicare obesity coverage pathway → NO SUPPORTING PASSAGE FOUND.
    The only "matches" are rows in a list of MLN newsletter titles, none about
    GLP-1s.
  - c2 (must): CMS announced an Innovation Center model for GLP-1 coverage
    (Medicaid and Part D) with staged start dates → NO SUPPORTING PASSAGE FOUND.
  - c3 (must): "Effective dates and eligibility criteria are stated with
    sources" → NO SUPPORTING PASSAGE FOUND. This one is also not really a claim:
    it describes how the answer should look, which breaks docs/08 §5 ("check
    presence, not style").

  Required evidence
  - e1 (press release, Nov 2025; key phrases GLP-1, Medicare) → not found. GLP-1
    only matched the title of a June 2026 newsletter, and Medicare only matched
    page boilerplate.
  - e2 (Innovation Center model announcement; Part D) → not found.

      11 +# Coming Soon: CMS to Provide $50 Monthly Access to GLP-1 Medic
         +ations for Medicare Beneficiaries                              
      12 +                                                               
      13 +Share                                                          
      14 +                                                               
      15 +**Coming Soon: CMS to Provide $50 Monthly Access to GLP-1 Medic
         +ations for Medicare Beneficiaries**                            
      16 +*Program Begins July 2026, Expanding Affordable Access to Innov
         +ative but Costly Treatments for Seniors*                       
      17 +                                                               
      18 +The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) will provide
         + eligible Medicare beneficiaries access to certain GLP-1 medica
         +tions for $50 per month beginning July 1, 2026, through Decembe
         +r 31, 2027.                                                    
      19 +                                                               
      20 +Under the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge, a time-limited demonstration, 
         +CMS is expanding access to innovative, evidence-based weight-lo
         +ss treatments. Eligible individuals enrolled in Medicare Part D
         + prescription drug plans will be able to access these medicatio
         +ns at a predictable and affordable cost-$50 for a monthly suppl
         +y. This approach reflects CMS' continued focus on improving acc
         +ess to high-value treatments that support better long-term heal
         +th outcomes.                                                   
      21 +                                                               
      22 +"These treatments are a major medical advancement, but too many
         + seniors are currently unable to access them due to high cost,"
         + **said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz**. "The Medicare GLP-1 
         +Bridge changes that by making these medications more affordable
         + and accessible, while advancing our broader goal of helping Am
         +ericans live healthier lives."                                 
      23 +                                                               
      24 +"GLP-1s can be life-changing for patients managing obesity and 
         +related conditions," **said Chris Klomp, Director of Medicare a
         +nd Chief Counselor at the U.S. Department of Health and Human S
         +ervices**. "This demonstration is designed to make accessing th
         +ose medications simpler, more predictable, and more consistent 
         +across the Medicare program, which means better quality of life
         + for seniors and better value across the health care system."  
      25 +                                                               
      26 +The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge operates under the Secretary's author
         +ity to test new approaches to care delivery under Medicare and 
         +is supported by CMS, including centralized processes for claims
         + adjudication and payment to pharmacies. This structure allows 
         +CMS to expand access while working closely with providers, phar
         +macies, and other partners to support a consistent and coordina
         +ted experience for patients.                                   
      27 +                                                               
      28 +**What to know before July 1**                                 
      29 +Beginning July 1, Medicare beneficiaries with Part D coverage m
         +ay be eligible to access certain GLP-1 medications at $50 for a
         + monthly supply. Beneficiaries can talk to their doctor to dete
         +rmine whether a GLP-1 medication is right for them. CMS will sh
         +are additional information for beneficiaries as the program beg
         +ins.                                                           
      30 +                                                               
      31 +In addition, CMS continues to work with stakeholders-including 
         +providers, pharmacies, and manufacturers-to support implementat
         +ion and ensure all partners have the information they need ahea
         +d of launch.                                                   
      32 +                                                               
      33 +The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge builds on CMS' broader efforts to imp
         +rove access to innovative therapies and support healthier outco
         +mes for Medicare beneficiaries. For additional demonstration de
         +tails, visit:                                                  
      34 +[https://www.cms.gov/medicare/coverage/prescription-drug-covera
         +ge/medicare-glp-1-bridge](/medicare/coverage/prescription-drug-
         +coverage/medicare-glp-1-bridge)                                
      35 +

      37 +

         +, sign up for CMS news [via email](mailto:press@cms.hhs.gov) an
         +d follow CMS on X [@CMSgov](https://x.com/CMSGov)

      10 +                                                               
      11 +# CMS Launches Voluntary Model to Expand Access to Life-Changin
         +g Medicines, Promote Healthier Living                          
      12 +                                                               
      13 +Share                                                          
      14 +                                                               
      15 +**CMS Launches Voluntary Model to Expand Access to Life-Changin
         +g Medicines, Promote Healthier Living**                        
      16 +*Model test enables state Medicaid agencies, Medicare Part D sp
         +onsors to cover GLP-1 drugs while controlling costs*           
      17 +                                                               
      18 +The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced to
         +day a new voluntary test of a model that is designed to enable 
         +Medicare Part D plans and state Medicaid agencies to cover GLP-
         +1 medications used for weight management and metabolic health i
         +mprovement, while helping control costs for patients and taxpay
         +ers.                                                           
      19 +                                                               
      20 +The Better Approaches to Lifestyle and Nutrition for Comprehens
         +ive hEalth (BALANCE) Model builds on emerging evidence that com
         +bines access to GLP-1 medications with access to evidence-based
         + lifestyle supports to achieve better long-term health outcomes
         +. The model represents a major step toward potential expanded a
         +ccess and affordability for millions of Americans.             
      21 +                                                               
      22 +"Today's announcement builds upon our historic Most Favored Nat
         +ions drug pricing deals' goal of democratizing access to weight
         +-loss medication, which has been out of reach for so many in ne
         +ed," said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. "These actions furth
         +er the administration's [bold plan](https://www.hhs.gov/maha/in
         +dex.html) to reform our country's health systems and Make Ameri
         +ca Healthy Again. With the BALANCE Model, we're pairing breakth
         +rough science with healthy living to cut costs while empowering
         + Americans to take control of their health."                   
      23 +                                                               
      24 +Under the model, CMS negotiates directly with pharmaceutical ma
         +nufacturers of GLP-1 drugs for lower net prices and standardize
         +d coverage terms. Negotiation areas include:                   
      25 +                                                               
      26 +"The BALANCE Model will empower more Americans to live healthie
         +r lives by expanding access to GLP-1s that have shown to be a p
         +owerful tool against the development of diseases, such as diabe
         +tes, cardiovascular disease, and other metabolic conditions, wh
         +ich can negatively affect a person's long-term health," CMS Inn
         +ovation Center Director Abe Sutton said. "Through this model, C
         +MS will make GLP-1s more accessible for people with Medicare an
         +d Medicaid."                                                   
      27 +                                                               
      28 +Participation will be voluntary for manufacturers, states, and 
         +plans. Additional information will be released in early 2026 re
         +garding state and Part D plan participation. The BALANCE Model 
         +will launch in Medicaid as early as May 2026 and in Medicare Pa
         +rt D in January 2027.                                          
      29 +                                                               
      30 +CMS has issued a Request for Applications to manufacturers, whi
         +ch are due January 8, 2026. Additionally, CMS has issued notice
         +s of intent for state Medicaid agencies and Medicare Part D pla
         +ns, which are also due January 8, 2026.                        
      31 +                                                               
      32 +The CMS Innovation Center will rigorously evaluate the model's 
         +impact on costs, adherence, outcomes, and beneficiary experienc
         +e to determine whether it improves health and generates savings
         +.                                                              
      33 +                                                               
      34 +To learn more about the BALANCE Model, visit: [https://www.cms.
         +gov/priorities/innovation/innovation-models/balance](/prioritie
         +s/innovation/innovation-models/balance).                       
      35 +                                                               
      36 +Prior to the launch of the BALANCE model, CMS also plans to imp
         +lement a new Medicare GLP-1 payment demonstration beginning in 
         +July 2026, which will serve as a short-term bridge to the model
         +. This additional payment demonstration means that Medicare ben
         +eficiaries can start accessing these important medications at p
         +rices negotiated by the Administration as soon as possible.    
      37 +                                                               
      38 +The GLP-1 payment demonstration will operate outside of the Med
         +icare Part D benefit's coverage and payment flow, which means t
         +hat Part D Plan Sponsors will not carry risk for eligible GLP-1
         + products furnished under the demonstration. Beneficiaries enro
         +lled in Medicare Part D who meet the negotiated access criteria
         + will have access to these drugs. Under the demonstration eligi
         +ble Medicare beneficiaries will pay $50 for a month of GLP-1 me

● I rewrote the glp1-path-005 answer key from CMS pages. Its original three
  flags are cleared, and the full test suite (409 passed) and ruff both pass. I
  have not marked it validated, and nothing is committed.

  What CMS actually says, and how the key changed

  The draft described a Novo Nordisk / Eli Lilly deal plus an Innovation Center
  model starting in Part D in January 2027. The CMS pages describe two programs,
  and one date has already changed since the announcement:

  #: c1
  Claim (new key): CMS announced the BALANCE Model, a voluntary Innovation
  Center
  model for GLP-1s in Medicaid and Part D
  must: ✓
  Verbatim source: BALANCE press release
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  #: c2
  Claim (new key): BALANCE launches in Medicaid "as early as May 2026"
  must: ✓
  Verbatim source: press release ¶13, BALANCE page ¶84
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  #: c3
  Claim (new key): Part D beneficiaries get access through the Medicare GLP-1 
  Bridge, "$50 per month beginning July 1, 2026"
  must: ✓
  Verbatim source: Bridge press release ¶8
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  #: c4
  Claim (new key): BALANCE is not launching in Medicare in 2027 (the original
  announcement said January 2027); the Bridge is extended through Dec 31, 2027
  must: ✓
  Verbatim source: Bridge providers page ¶72–73 (revised 2026-04-06), BALANCE
  page ¶95–96
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  #: c5
  Claim (new key): Bridge eligibility: prior authorization, weight-loss use
  only;
  people with type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea or MASH get GLP-1s through their
  Part D plan instead
  must:
  Verbatim source: providers page ¶79, ¶84
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  #: c6
  Claim (new key): The Bridge runs outside the Part D benefit, so plans carry no

  risk
  must:
  Verbatim source: providers page ¶71

  - Evidence: e1 is the BALANCE press release, e2 the Bridge providers page
    (both must), e3 the Bridge press release. Every key phrase matched verbatim
    in its page.
  - Expected contradiction: the launch press release gives Part D January 2027,
    but the current pages say not in 2027. The current pages govern.
  - Forbidden: "BALANCE covers GLP-1s in Part D starting January 2027"; "Part D
    plans cover GLP-1s for obesity as a standard benefit".
  - Dropped: the Novo Nordisk / Eli Lilly agreement, because no CMS or HHS page
    I fetched names the manufacturers. The BALANCE release only mentions "Most
    Favored Nations drug pricing deals".

  The two remaining flags are expected: prose forbidden claims can't be checked
  automatically, the same as nine other records.

  Two fixes to fetch_sources, so re-running it confirms a fix

  - Canonical URLs are fetched directly. docs/08 §5 allows URLs in
    governing_documents, but the script sent every non-LCD/article entry to
    search. The flags on a corrected key could never have cleared.
  - Dates on press releases and fact sheets are checked by whether they appear 
    in the text. The script compared July 1, 2026 with each page's last-revised
    date and raised four date flags on a correct key. LCD and article dates are
    still compared as before, so the four existing L33822/A52464 date flags
    remain.

  The re-run brought total flags from 47 to 46, and no other record's flags or
  worksheet changed. Both fixes have tests and entries in the decision log.

     pathway exists for GLP-1s used for obesity, and when does it take effect?"

  1. glp1-path-005 · glp1 · T3 · coverage_pathway · train · ✅ validated

  Q: What Medicare coverage pathway for GLP-1s used for obesity was announced in
  late 2025, and when does it take effect?
  Summary: CMS announced the BALANCE Model, a voluntary Innovation Center model
  for Medicaid and Part D; it launches in Medicaid as early as May 2026. Part D
  beneficiaries get access through the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge instead: $50/month
  from July 1, 2026, outside the Part D benefit, with prior authorization. The
  original announcement put BALANCE in Part D in January 2027; CMS now says it
  is not launching in Medicare in 2027 and has extended the Bridge through
  December 31, 2027.
  - c1 (must) BALANCE Model announced: voluntary Innovation Center model,
    Medicaid + Part D, GLP-1s for weight management
  - c2 (must) BALANCE launches in Medicaid as early as May 2026
  - c3 (must) Part D access via the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge, $50/month from July
    1, 2026
  - c4 (must) BALANCE not launching in Part D in 2027 (originally January 2027);
    Bridge extended through Dec 31, 2027
  - c5 Bridge eligibility: eligible plan type, weight-loss use only, prior
    authorization; people with T2D/OSA/MASH use their Part D plan instead
  - c6 Bridge runs outside Part D's coverage and payment flow; plans carry no
    risk
  - Evidence: e1 (must) BALANCE press release · e2 (must) Bridge providers page
    · e3 Bridge "Coming Soon" press release
  - Contradictions: launch release said Part D in January 2027 vs the current
    pages · trade-press timelines
  - Forbidden: f1 "BALANCE covers GLP-1s in Part D starting Jan 2027" · f2 "Part
    D plans cover GLP-1s for obesity as a standard benefit"
  - Flags (2): f1 and f2 verify by hand

  7. cgm-elig-001 · cgm · T2 · eligibility · train · draft

  Q: Is a therapeutic CGM covered under Medicare for a type 2 diabetic who is
  not on insulin?
  Summary: Yes, potentially. Under LCD L33822 a CGM is covered for a beneficiary
  with diabetes who is either treated with insulin OR has a history of
  problematic hypoglycemia (recurrent level 2 or at least one level 3 event)
  despite attempts to modify treatment, plus practitioner visit and
  documentation requirements. A non-insulin patient qualifies only through the
  hypoglycemia pathway.
  - c1 (must) Coverage requires treatment with insulin OR a documented history
    of problematic hypoglycemia
  - c2 (must) Problematic hypoglycemia means recurrent level 2 events or at
    least one level 3 event, despite multiple attempts to adjust medication or
    modify the treatment plan
  - c3 (must) A visit with the treating practitioner to evaluate diabetes
    control and determine the CGM criteria are met, within the required window
    before the order
  - c4 The non-insulin pathway was introduced by the LCD revision effective
    April 16, 2023
  - Evidence: e1 (must) L33822, phrases problematic hypoglycemia, insulin
  - Forbidden: f1 "Multiple daily injections (three or more) are required"
    (removed by the 2023 revision)
  - Flags (1): currency note only (L33822 is now 2024-10-01; the 2023 row is
    still in its history, so c4 is fine)
  - Watch: c2 uses "level 2"/"level 3", which record 8 found are not in L33822.

● It's a deliberate rule in this project, not a malfunction.
  .claude/settings.json denies me reading or editing .env:

  "deny": ["Read(.env)", "Read(**/.env)", "Edit(.env)", "Write(.env)", ...]

  The guard-paths.sh hook separately blocks any write to .env. My grep on .env
  counted as a read, so it was refused. The point is to keep your API keys out
  of my context and out of LangSmith traces. That's also why the Day 1 log says
  only you can fix PRIME_MODELS__SUB.

  It matters for the judge switch. If .env sets PRIME_MODELS__JUDGE, that value
  overrides the new default and the switch would silently do nothing. You can
  check without showing me any keys; this prints only variable names:

  ! grep -o "^PRIME_MODELS__[A-Z_]*" .env

     Plan — task 2.2: judge and critic (docs/09 §2.2)

     Context

     Judge and critic are pass-through stubs (agents/graph.py L324–334) and
     every run is one search round. 2.2 gives them models and prompts, wires the
     docs/03 §1 conditional edges (judge → re-search, critic → one more round),
     adds deadline/budget checks at every node, and must pass the check: on
     adv-cgm-001 ("Is a CGM covered by Medicare for gestational diabetes?") the
     run shows a judge round or a critic recommendation and the answer's
     Contradictions section is non-empty.

     Exploration found round 2 is broken today in five ways, which this task
     must fix first:
     - budget_remaining() subtracts agents run-wide, so after a 6-agent round 0
       later rounds get 0 agents.
     - collect zips the accumulating task_results against running tasks, so
       round-1 results get paired with round-0 tasks.
     - dispatch re-seeds the plan whenever pending_tasks is empty.
     - Sub-agents never check the run deadline.
     - Nothing persists verdicts or critic reports.

     It also found that contradictions have no route into the answer: the claim
     graph flags only same-branch conflicts, and cross-branch detection is
     roadmap R3.

     User decisions (binding):
     1. Critic findings feed synthesis; Answer.contradictions becomes readable
        one-liners.
     2. max_rounds counts all search rounds including the initial one; the
        critic's single re-search is allowed beyond it if searches, tokens and
        the deadline allow.
     3. max_agents is a per-round cap.

     Defaults I'm taking (logged in docs/11):
     - The judge still runs at fast depth (spec draws it on every path; V4-Flash
       ≈1.6 s), but its tasks are ignored; the critic is skipped at fast (03
       §10).
     - A failed judge records sufficient=False with no tasks (routing identical;
       never claims a sufficiency it didn't check).
     - Outdated sources go to the synthesis notes, not to Answer.contradictions.

     Commits (small, in order)

     1. fix: round plumbing for multi-round runs

     - workspace.py
       - budget_remaining().max_agents = limit.max_agents (per round).
         usage.agents stays a run total for reporting.
       - New fields verdicts: list[Verdict] and critic_reports: 
         list[CriticReport], included in to_record, so _persist saves them at
         every node.
       - charge_tokens(message, prompt=None) moved from synthesizer._charge,
         which now calls it.
     - graph.py
       - New state key results_by_task: Annotated[dict[str, TaskResult], merge],
         set by _search_agent on both paths. collect pairs results by task id
         for tasks of the current round; _unknowns reads t.result from ws.tasks.
       - _dispatch seeds from the plan only when round == 0 and not ws.tasks.
         max_agents = min(ws.budget.max_agents, DEPTH cap, 
         remaining.max_searches).
       - _slice_budget floor: max(min(1, r), r // share), so no phantom budget.
       - _search_agent skips the sub-agent when past the deadline, returning a
         failed result "not started: run deadline reached".
       - _can_search(ws, state): the deadline has not passed; searches and
         tokens remain; at least MIN_SECONDS_FOR_ROUND = 30 s are left.
       - Named RECURSION_LIMIT = 50 with the worst-case arithmetic (≈21
         supersteps) in a comment.
     - Round arithmetic
       - state["round"] = completed search rounds (collect sets round+1;
         usage.rounds equals it).
       - Tasks created after collect get round = state["round"].
       - Deep: r0 → judge may add r1, r2 (round < 3) → critic may add one r3 →
         judge (no tasks) → critic, second and last run → synthesize.
       - Fast: r0 → judge (tasks ignored) → synthesize.
     - config.py / docs/01 §3: max_rounds and max_agents comments.
     - Tests (test_graph.py, test_workspace.py):
       - no re-seeding after round 0; round 2 gets its full agent cap; results
         paired by task id across rounds; no searches left dispatches nothing;
         budget_remaining no longer spends agents run-wide; to_record carries
         verdicts and reports.
       - Existing whole-graph tests now stub run_judge and run_critic.

     2. feat: judge node and conditional re-search edge

     - New agents/judge.py
       - run_judge(ws, *, judged_round, max_rounds, per_round_agents, 
         prompt_set, model=None) -> JudgeOutcome(verdict, mode, fallback_tag, 
         error).
       - Calls models.structured("judge", Verdict), or
         model.with_structured_output when a test injects one. The native ×2 →
         fenced JSON ladder is the 01 §9 repair.
     - models.StructuredCaller
       - Records last_message: native rung via with_structured_output(schema, 
         include_raw=True), plus the fenced rung's message; tokens are charged
         from it.
       - If include_raw is unsupported on ChatNebius (verified by smoke), fall
         back to estimating from the prompt and output and tag tokens:estimated.
     - _normalize_verdict
       - Coverage: keep known branch ids; fill missing ones as partial or
         unresolved from evidence.
       - Tasks: drop resolved, unknown or empty-instruction tasks and tasks
         repeating an issued query; sufficient means no tasks; cap at min(3, 
         per_round_agents), queries_hint ≤ 3, include_domains as bare hosts.
       - The harness rewrites task_id ({branch}-r{round}[-k]), round, status and
         result.
     - Failure: sufficient=False, empty tasks, an error event with node="judge",
       tag fallback:judge_failed.
     - prompts/judge.md
       - Placeholders: {question} {stop_criteria} {branches} {unresolved} 
         {budget} {round} {max_new_tasks}.
       - Branch blocks list claims with status, governing date, for/against
         counts and best tier; tasks already run with their queries; the
         unresolved note.
       - Rubric resolved/partial/unresolved (04 §1 tiers); when to stop;
         no-duplicate and no-resolved-branch rules; output fields; a neutral
         example (no CGM facts).
     - graph._judge
       - Emits verdict and appends it to ws.verdicts.
       - Sets pending_tasks = verdict.new_tasks only if insufficient, round < 
         max_rounds, depth ≠ fast and _can_search. Otherwise it clears new_tasks
         in the recorded verdict and logs judge.tasks_ignored.
     - Tests (test_judge.py):
       - the prompt carries stop criteria, claims with dates, unresolved notes
         and budget; resolved-branch tasks dropped; cap of 3; ids, round and
         status rewritten; duplicate query dropped; sufficient means no tasks;
         coverage filled; failure gives tag and error event; tokens charged.
       - test_structured.py: last_message recorded, stub accepts include_raw.

     3. feat: critic node with one re-search round

     - New agents/critic.py: run_critic(ws, *, state_round, final_review, 
       prompt_set, model=None) -> CriticOutcome(report|None, mode, fallback_tag,
       error).
     - Ladder (planner precedent in root.plan_run):
       a. critic_model() fenced JSON → parse_fenced_json → CriticReport.
       b. One repair turn via new prompts/critic_repair.md.
       c. structured("judge", CriticReport), tag fallback:critic_structured.
       d. None, with an error event and tag fallback:critic_skipped.

       - Known claim ids only; outdated_sources external ids mapped to doc ids.
       - contradictions = known claim ids or one-line descriptions of at least
         20 characters.
       - Probability clamped to [0, 1]; ≤ 3 recommended searches.
       - An unknown branch becomes the pseudo-branch critic; ids

     - prompts/critic.md
       - Adversarial stance, grounded only in what's shown.
       - The six 03 §7 questions, each mapped to its field;

       - Exactly one fenced json block.
       - Inputs: claims with ≤ 3 supporting and ≤ 3 contradicting evidence lines
         (id, tier, external id, dates, passage clipped to 300 chars);
         documents with tiers, dates and supersession; contested ids; trajectory
         per branch; latest coverage and missing items; review mode.
     - graph._critic
       - Skips on deadline, fast depth or critic_rounds >= 2; otherwise runs,

       - Dispatches only if the report exists, probability < 0.7, critic_rounds 
         == 0, tasks are non-empty and _can_search (beyond max_rounds, per
         decision 2).
     - Edges (every router sends an expired deadline to synthesize, replacing
       docs/11 L252's no-op approach):

     | Router            | Targets                                          |
     |-------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
     | _after_understand | plan / synthesize                                |
     | _after_plan       | dispatch / synthesize                            |
     | _fan_out          | Sends / collect / synthesize                     |
     | _after_collect    | judge / synthesize                               |
     | _after_judge      | dispatch if pending / critic / synthesize (fast) |
     | _after_critic     | dispatch if pending / synthesize                 |
       Nodes keep their own deadline no-ops for direct calls.
     - Tests (test_critic.py, test_graph.py):
       - Critic: fenced JSON parse; repair turn; structured fallback tag; total
         failure skipped with an error event; ids and critic suffix;
         pseudo-branch; unknown ids dropped but descriptions kept; the prompt
         shows evidence, tiers, dates and queries.
       - Graph: insufficient with rounds left → dispatch; no rounds left →
         critic with tasks ignored; fast never re-searches or critiques (final
         round 1); critic below threshold dispatches once then returns to the
         judge; critic at most twice; critic round allowed beyond max_rounds but
         not without budget; expired deadline sends every router to synthesize
         (parametrized); worst-case deep run under the recursion limit; verdicts
         and reports reach state.json.

● The spec review found the core design sound: no routing loops, results pair
  correctly across rounds, the recursion limit holds, and the three planning
  decisions are implemented and logged. It also found real gaps. Most I can fix
  now; one needs your decision.

  Fixing now:
  1. Verdicts can list tasks that never run. The judge may propose 3 tasks when
     dispatch can only afford 1. Judge, critic and dispatch will share one
     per-round cap.
  2. The answer body gets uncited sentences. docs/03 §8 requires every factual
     sentence to be cited. Inserted bullets will carry their passages'
     citations, and the critic's free-text sentences stay out of the body; they
     remain in Answer.contradictions.
  3. A judge answering via the fenced-JSON fallback isn't tagged, which docs/06
     §2 requires.
  4. Failed structured-output attempts aren't charged to the token budget.
  5. Doc and comment slips: a duplicated agents line in docs/02 and a stale
     comment in schemas.py.
  6. Missing tests: critic token charging, and a real critic's task going
     through dispatch.

  Needs your decision (after the fixes): when the token budget is spent, docs/01
  §9 says jump straight to synthesis, but the judge and critic currently still
  run. Applied strictly, that rule would stop them in every live deep run today.

  Also, commit c2db120 Delete OPERATOR_GUIDE.md sits in the 2.2 range and isn't
  mine; I've left it alone.

  I'll write all the fixes as one patch script.

      128 +**As built (task 2.3), report.** `eval/report.py --split holdo
          +ut|dev [--passes N]` reads only `reports/bench/*.json`, so it 
          +costs nothing to regenerate. Holdout goes to `reports/final-re
          +port.md` and any other split to `reports/<split>-report.md`. E
          +xperiments are grouped by configuration `<mode>-<prompt_set>-<
          +depth>`, keeping the latest N passes of each; with N ≥ 2 a met
          +ric shows the mean of the per-pass means ± half their range. S
          +ubset (`--ids`) runs are never counted. Not-applicable scores 
          +are left out of means, and a metric with no value renders as `
          +—`. A coverage line says whether all 12 keys have at least one
          + value for every configuration, and names the gaps. The report
          + states the Tavily cache per configuration and flags dev as a 
          +build-time check, not a result. Sections: configurations (expe
          +riment links, git sha, evaluator, dataset sha), coverage, head
          +line, PRD §9 targets on their subsets (tier 4 contradiction ha
          +ndling, change-detection currency, recall, citation correctnes
          +s, answer-correctness delta over the baseline), per tier, per 
          +domain, per question (with trace links), worked examples (lowe
          +st-tier, contradiction and out-of-scope records, with excerpts
          + from each config), cost and latency (agent and judge tokens),
          + and evaluator comments. It also writes `reports/latest.json`:
          + `{generated_at, split, passes, sources, configs: [{config, mo
          +de, prompt_set, depth, split, experiments: [{name, url, tavily
          +_cache, git_sha, evaluator_model, dataset_sha, started_at, res
          +cored_at, file}], n, metrics: {key: {mean, spread, n}}, compos
          +ite, per_tier, per_domain, judge_errors, failed_runs, judge_to
          +kens, missing_keys}], prd_targets: [{config, metric, subset, v
          +alue, n, target, met}]}`. The file reflects the last split rep
          +orted.

  Evaluator bugs found on the live runs and fixed, each with a regression test
  and a docs/11 line:
  - When the judge left out its claims list, every claim was graded missing. Two
    correct baseline answers scored 0.2.
  - Prime token counts are above LangSmith's score limit, so LangSmith dropped
    whole batches of scores.
  - Baseline citations in [^id^] footnote style, or under ### headings, weren't
    counted.
  - The citation judge failed sentences that named their source's document id or
    date, because it never saw which document a passage came from. It also
    graded the "Effective dates relied on" list as if it were claims.
  - A Wegovy label cited from DailyMed didn't match the key's fda.gov label.
  - The evaluator model spent its whole default 8,192-token output allowance
    thinking and returned empty replies, so its output limit is now 32k.

  Things you should know
  - Judge scores vary between runs. Rescoring the same baseline answers moved
    two answer-correctness scores by 0.3–0.5 each. With 5 questions, that shifts
    a config's average by about 0.1. Before the holdout run, choose between a
    majority of 3 judge calls per metric and averaging repeated bench runs
    (--passes N).
  - Prime is less correct than the baseline on dev (0.68 vs 0.87). On
    glp1-path-002 prime said Wegovy isn't covered, based on an unrelated Part B
    exclusion article.
  - Other prime problems:
    - notes from the critic step ("The reviewer flagged…") leak into answers;
    - 3 of 5 runs ran out of token budget;
    - some cited passages don't back the sentence citing them.

    These are product issues outside 2.3. They can go in a small fix round

     Plan — task 2.4: API (docs/09 §2.4)

     Context

     2.3 is approved. 2.5 builds the Next.js compare view, and it needs an HTTP
     API. Its types come from this API's
     OpenAPI schema. docs/09 §2.4: "api/main.py: all endpoints; events.py with
     SSE queue + JSONL; run persistence;
     feedback to LangSmith + file; /ui-event. Check: curl a run, stream its
     events, fetch its record, post
     feedback (verify in LangSmith)." No [G] gate. Specs: 01 §2 and §8, 02 §4–5,
     05 §4, 06 §2–4 and §8, 07 §3, §7 and §9.

     Exploration found three problems the API would hit, each fixed first in its
     own commit:
     - Tracing off breaks runs. tracing.trace_run always posts a RunTree, and
       TraceHandle.__init__ calls
       get_url(), which reads the project over the network. With no LangSmith
       key a run likely fails in trace_run.
       07 §9 and §10 require the UI and API to work with tracing off.
     - Feedback has no trace to target. create_feedback needs a trace/run id,
       but only langsmith_run_url is stored.
     - Replay and live can overlap. events.emit appends under the lock and
       publishes after releasing it, so a
       new SSE subscriber can get an event twice, with nothing to dedupe on.

     Other facts:
     - run_prime/run_baseline are synchronous. They accept ws= (so run_id exists
       before the run starts) and
       source=. They emit token through events.emit as well as on_token, so
       subscribing is enough. Both emit
       error + run.finished, then re-raise.
     - eval/run_eval.make_target already pre-builds the Workspace and runs
       benches concurrently.
     - The baseline's run.started lacks depth, which the 02 §4 contract
       requires.
     - events.run_dir() creates directories. Lookups must use runs_root()/id.
     - Installed: fastapi 0.141, sse-starlette 3.4, uvicorn 0.52, httpx 0.28
       (transitive only).

     Decisions

     User (binding):
     1. RunRecord.langsmith_trace_id: str | None = None, written by prime and
        baseline from the trace handle.
        Schema change, so docs/02 §2.1 is updated in the same commit. Runs
        without it get file-only feedback.
     2. Events gain a per-run seq, assigned under the append lock. It is the SSE
        id:, so a reconnect with
        Last-Event-ID resumes. For old runs, replay fills seq from line order.
        docs/02 §4 and 06 §4 are updated.
     3. data/feedback.jsonl and data/ui-events.jsonl are gitignored.
     4. PHI guard on POST /run questions and feedback comments rejects DOB,
        MRN/member id/policy no, and a named
        patient (422 with a clear message). "A1c <number>" is allowed, since
        policy questions quote thresholds.

     Defaults (each logged in docs/11):
     - Runs execute on a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) owned by the app
       lifespan. There is no cancellation
       (the spec has none); in-flight runs finish or die with the process.
     - A saved status="running" that the in-process registry doesn't know is
       reported by /runs as
       interrupted. The SSE stream for such a run ends with a stream-only error
       + run.finished {status: failed}
       that is never written to disk.
     - CORS allows http://localhost:3000 and http://127.0.0.1:3000. The UI proxy
       is 2.5's, but Next dev
       rewrites can buffer SSE.
     - /runs also lists runs/examples/*, for reviewers without keys.
     - API-only request/response models live in prime_search/api/models.py, not
       in schemas.py. schemas.py
       stays the agent/record contract; 07 §7 documents the API shapes.
     - A feedback POST maps to up to three LangSmith keys (06 §3): user_thumbs
       (score 1/0, with the comment),
       user_comment (comment only, when given) and user_flagged_claims (comment
       = ids). It also writes one
       JSONL line. The LangSmith call runs off the event loop and never fails
       the request; {ok, langsmith} reports it.
     - httpx is added as a dev dependency, because TestClient needs it.

     in tests/test_event_contract.py.

       - start(request) builds Workspace(objective,

     - prime_search/api/sse.py: stream(run_id, last_event_id).
       a. Subscribe first. The callback runs
          loop.call_soon_threadsafe(queue.put_nowait, record).
       b. Replay the file past last, off-loop. Stop at run.finished.

          +t once (the `eval/run_eval.make_target` pattern), then runs on
          + a 4-worker thread pool: two compare-view questions at a time,
          + with further runs queued. There is no cancellation; the spec 
          +has none, and a LangGraph run can't be stopped from outside. R
          +uns are tagged `source:ui` (06 §2). A runner that dies before 
          +emitting `run.finished` gets `error` + `run.finished {status: 
          +failed}` and a failed record from the API, so no stream waits 
          +forever — 01 §2, 07 §3

          +is derived and never written. The SSE stream for such a run en
          +ds with an `error` and a `run.finished {status: failed}` that 
          +are sent without an `id` and never written, so the record stay
          +s as the run left it. A run started by another process (the CL
          +I) is treated the same once it stops emitting. Runs under `run
          +s/examples/` are listed with `example: true`. CORS allows `loc
          +alhost:3000`/`127.0.0.1:3000`, because a Next dev rewrite can

      356  - 2026-09-13 — Task 2.4: API run execution. Each `POST /run` b
           uilds its `Workspace` before starting, so `{run_id}` returns a
           t once (the `eval/run_eval.make_target` pattern), then runs on
            a 4-worker thread pool: two compare-view questions at a time,
            with further runs queued. There is no cancellation; the spec 
           has none, and a LangGraph run can't be stopped from outside. R
           uns are tagged `source:ui` (06 §2). A runner that dies before 
           emitting `run.finished` gets `error` + `run.finished {status: 
           failed}` and a failed record from the API, so no stream waits 
           forever — 01 §2, 07 §3

           ds with an `error` and a `run.finished {status: failed}` that

● The spec review found one blocker, one should-fix, a nit and three test gaps.
  All are worth fixing before I report 2.4 done:
  - Blocker, live events can be lost. emit assigns seq under the lock but
    publishes after releasing it. Two prime sub-agents emitting at once can
    publish 6 before 5, and the stream then drops 5 for good, even on reconnect.
    - Fix: append and publish in one critical section on an RLock, with
      subscribers kept under their own small lock. Subscribers then always
      receive events in seq order.
  - Should-fix, completed runs look failed on reconnect. A browser that
    reconnects with the last event's id got a fake "run interrupted" banner.
    - Fix: a run.finished the client already has ends the stream quietly.
  - Nit, runs started outside the API end too early. A run from the CLI was
    called interrupted after any 1-second gap between events.
    - Fix: it counts as interrupted only once its events file has been quiet for
      180 seconds.
  - Test gaps:
    - The mid-run SSE test didn't guarantee the client joined before the
      remaining events. It now waits until the stream has subscribed, and the
      fake runner emits the second batch from several threads.
    - New tests: in-order delivery to subscribers, reconnecting past the final
      event, streaming a run only other processes write to, and a baseline run
      with tracing really off.

  Private list:
  1. Rewrite prime_search/api/sse.py with the reconnect and 180-second fixes.
  2. Write a patch script for the events.py lock change, the test updates, and
     the docs/06 §4 and docs/11 lines.

           "down"`, since 07 §7 names the field but no type, and maps it 
           to `user_thumbs` 1/0. One POST writes up to three LangSmith ke
           ys (06 §3). They go to the root trace as `run_id=<trace id>`: 
           a root run's id is its trace id, and `run_id` makes the call s
           ynchronous, so `{ok, langsmith}` reports whether LangSmith has
            it (passing `trace_id` queues it in the background). The loca
           l line is written even when LangSmith is skipped or fails, and
            it carries question and mode, so `from_feedback.py` needs no 
           join against `runs/`. A failed file write is a 500, because a 
           dropped feedback line is a lost signal. The two JSONL files ar
           e ignored by `data/.gitignore` (user decision), not the root `
           .gitignore`, which has an unrelated uncommitted edit — 05 §4, 
           06 §3, §8

● Task 2.4, the API, is built and committed. It ran end to end against real
  runs, and both points the spec review raised in the event stream are fixed
  (31832bc). 619 tests pass and ruff is clean. There's no gate on 2.4, so this
  is where it stands.

  Live check, run on port 8765 (port 8000 is unavailable, see below):
  - Runs: a baseline and a prime fast run started together and each returned its
    id immediately. Both event streams ran to run.finished; the baseline's
    reached id 168 and prime's 146.
  - Reconnect: resuming with Last-Event-ID: 3 started at id 4.
  - Records: both came back with the new LangSmith trace id, which matches the
    one in the trace URL. The runs list showed them newest first, with the prime
    run still running while it was in progress.
  - Document view: a fetched document opened as 275 paragraphs, shown a page at
    a time, with its 2 pieces of evidence.
  - Feedback: returned {"ok": true, "langsmith": true}. All three keys showed up
    on that run's trace in LangSmith, and the line landed in
    data/feedback.jsonl.
  - Everything else:
    - a question carrying a record number and date of birth was rejected with
      422;
    - UI events were written;
    - bench questions came back without answer keys, and the bench summary
      served the dev report.

  Built (10 commits, 5d190cc → 31832bc):
  - Fixes made first:
    - the baseline's start event now includes depth;
    - runs no longer fail when tracing is off;
    - records keep the LangSmith trace id;
    - every event carries a sequence number;
    - the patient-detail check is shared by the API and the dataset tooling.
  - API: runs and live event stream, run list and records, document view, bench
    questions and summary, feedback and UI events.
  - Docs: 07 §7, 01 §2, 02, 05, 06, a README curl example, and a test that keeps
    the API schema fully typed for 2.5.

  The spec review's findings, all fixed with tests:
  - Events could be lost for good: when two sub-agents emitted at the same
    moment, the stream could skip one. Events now always reach the stream in
    order.
  - Finished runs looked failed on reconnect: a browser reconnecting to a
    completed run was told it had been interrupted. It now closes quietly.
  - Other processes' runs were cut short: a run started outside the API, such as
    from the CLI, was marked interrupted after a one-second pause. It now
    counts as interrupted only after 180 seconds of silence.

  Decision for you before 2.5: Windows reserves port 8000 on this machine, so
  make dev-api can't start the API there. docs/01 §2, the Makefile and the
  planned UI proxy all assume 8000. Should I make the API port configurable, or
  change the default (for example to 8765)?

  Other things to know:
  - Tracing-off is covered by tests, including a real baseline run with tracing
    off. I didn't check it on the live server, because the LangSmith key is read
    from .env.
  - The prime fast run was thin: 1 search, 1 document, then it ran out of budget
    in about 30 seconds. That's how fast mode behaves, not the API, but it will
    be visible in the side-by-side view.
  - All commits are unpushed.
  - Still waiting on you:
    - the rename of PRIME_MODELS__SUB in .env;
    - the uncommitted .gitignore change, which I didn't touch; feedback files
      are ignored through data/.gitignore instead;
    - the untracked build-log/day1-transcript.md.

     Plan: task 2.5, the UI harness (docs/09 §2.5, docs/07)

     Context

     2.4 shipped the API, but ui/ is still the create-next-app placeholder
     (commit 79bfad0), so the 2.5 gate cannot run yet. docs/09 §2.5 asks for:
     - types from OpenAPI;
     - useRunEvents;
     - a compare view with both panes: search tree, answer with citation hover,
       evidence, claims, critic, usage footer, feedback;
     - /runs, /runs/[id] with a Plan tab, /docs/... and /bench.

     [G] A side-by-side run of a preset question works end to end in the
     browser, and the thumbs write to LangSmith. Specs: docs/07 (all sections),
     02 §2 and §4, 06 §5 and §8. The user started servers on :3000 (Next dev)
     and 127.0.0.1:8765 (API).

     What exploration found in code and real runs:
     - Plan event has no code. The plan event is a bare SearchPlan; the root's
       plan code stays a local variable in agents/root.py, but 07 §4's Plan tab
       needs it.
     - Prime usage stops early. Prime emits usage only in collect
       (graph.py:353). The judge, critic and synthesis tokens never reach the
       stream: run 01a09bb6's last usage event shows 333,448 input tokens
       against 341,970 in its record, although 06 §5 says usage and run.finished
       carry totals.
     - Streamed tokens differ from the answer. Streamed text uses 【n】
       brackets, gets sections injected, and may duplicate itself after a stream
       fallback. The answer event's body_markdown must replace it. That final
       body uses [n] markers with gaps, and its Sources URLs are indented 4
       spaces, which Markdown renders as code.
     - Baseline stream quirks. The baseline emits two search frames per tool
       call (the second has query:""), and writes its record only at the end.
     - Failed tasks look different. A failed task's task.done is flat ({task_id,
       branch_id, evidence:0, unresolved}).
     - No round-boundary event. A usage followed by a verdict marks the end of a
       round. Critic tasks are identified by the -critic{k} suffix on their
       task_id.
     - SSE frames are named events. Each frame has an event: type, so the client
       needs addEventListener per type (onmessage never fires). The stream must
       be closed on run.finished, or the browser reconnects to it.
       Last-Event-ID is only sent by the browser's own auto-reconnect.
     - Old runs are incomplete. Only the newest runs carry seq (replay fills it
       from line order), and some very old runs have no state.json.
     - The optimized prompt set doesn't exist yet. prompt_set: optimized has no
       prompts/optimized/ and silently falls back to base.
     - Types and dependencies. OpenAPI already carries every payload model
       through RunRecord: Answer, Branch, Citation, Claim, CriticReport,
       Evidence, QueryUnderstanding, SearchPlan, SearchTask, TaskResult, Usage,
       Verdict. The scaffold is Next 15.5.25, React 19.1, Tailwind 4.3,
       TypeScript 5.9 strict, ESLint 9 and pnpm 12.4 on Node 24. No test runner
       is installed.

     Decisions

     User (binding):
     1. The gate's live run is deep, about 2–3 min and ~450k tokens.
     2. next.config.ts reads PRIME_API_PORT / PRIME_API_HOST from the shell
        first, then parses only those two keys from the repo-root .env, then
        defaults to 127.0.0.1:8765.
     3. Fix both backend gaps first: code on the plan event, and final usage on
        the stream.
     4. Add react-markdown + remark-gfm and vitest.

     Defaults (each gets a docs/11 line):
     - REST goes through the /api rewrite. SSE connects directly to
       NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIME_API_ORIGIN: dev rewrites can buffer streams, and API
       CORS already allows :3000. A host of 0.0.0.0 maps to 127.0.0.1.
     - Types are generated to ui/src/types/api.ts (07 §8 says src/types.ts) and
       committed, so builds don't need the API running. pnpm gen:types
       regenerates them. The payload types OpenAPI lacks are hand-written in
       src/lib/events.ts: run.started, task.started, search, fetch, task.done,
       token, run.finished, error.
     - One pure reducer reduceRun(view, event) serves both the live stream and
       replay. The contract quirks above are absorbed there, not changed in the
       backend.
     - The "opt" prompt radio is rendered disabled, with the note "GEPA has not
       produced optimized prompts yet".
     - Feedback controls are enabled only after run.finished, because the record
       must exist for POST /feedback.
     - All pages are client components (a local API gains nothing from SSR).
       Styling is Tailwind only, following prefers-color-scheme: one accent
       colour for prime and neutral for baseline, with tier and status badges
       that always carry text labels (07 §10).

         plan|judge|critic, status, searches[], fetchDocIds[], result?,
         unresolved?}}, taskOrder, verdicts[], critiques[{afterRound, report}];
       - findings: evidence[] and evidenceById, fetches{doc_id → fetch payload},
         baselineSearches[];
       - answer: streamText, answer;
       - bookkeeping: usage, errors[], finished, lastSeq.
     - Event rules:
       - An event with seq <= lastSeq is dropped; events with no id are always
         applied.
       - origin comes from the -critic suffix, otherwise round > 0 means judge.
       - A search or fetch with a null task_id goes to the baseline list. A
         query:"" frame fills the oldest pending item for the same tool.
       - Both task.done shapes are handled.
       - verdict and critique are ordered by the latest usage.rounds.
       - answer replaces streamText.
       - run.finished sets status, trace URL, usage and finished.
     - Selectors: branchStatus, evidenceByBranch, timeline(). The timeline gives
       round-0 tasks by branch, then a separator, then later rounds, matching
       07 §3's ASCII.
     - Tests: src/lib/reducer.test.ts uses hand-made fixtures for every event
       type, both task.done shapes, baseline search pairing, seq dedup, answer
       replacing tokens, and critic origin. An optional replay of real
       ../runs/<id>/events.jsonl is skipped when absent.

     U4 ui: useRunEvents with replay fallback

     src/lib/useRunEvents.ts (useReducer, native EventSource at
     ${origin}/run/${id}/events):
     - One listener per event type; close on run.finished.
     - Transient errors are left to the browser's own reconnect, which sends
       Last-Event-ID.
     - If the stream is CLOSED before finishing: fetch GET /runs/{id}/events,
       apply it, then reopen (seq dedup drops repeats). Back off 1/2/4 s, at
       most 5 tries.
     - Clean up on unmount; this covers StrictMode's double mount.
     - On run.finished, invalidate and refetch GET /runs/{id} so the footer and
       feedback use the saved record.

     src/lib/useRun.ts (for /runs/[id]):
     - Load the JSON replay and the record.
     - Attach useRunEvents only if the replay has no run.finished; an
       interrupted run then receives the API's synthetic failure.

     U5 ui: compare view shell and QuestionBar

     - src/app/page.tsx: a two-pane grid, a "hide baseline" toggle (posts
       ui.compare_toggled), and per-pane error banners, with the other pane
       continuing (07 §3).
     - QuestionBar:
       - Question input, and presets from GET /bench/questions grouped by domain
         and tier, plus "custom" (a preset sets question_id).
       - Depth radio (deep default); prompts radio with "opt" disabled.
       - Ask sends POST /run twice concurrently. A 422 detail shows inline;
         asking again posts ui.rerun.
     - RunPane and PaneHeader: mode, model/tool line, understanding chips,
       status.

     U6 ui: search tree

     - Components: SearchTree, BranchNode, TaskNode, RoundSeparator.
     - Branch: status pending / running / done / failed, evidence count, and the
       task summary on expand.
     - Task: a round label and a critic badge, with search children (query, n
       results, cached) and fetch children (title, tier badge, effective date).
     - Separator: "round n: judge → sufficient | insufficient, k new tasks",
       with a critic line (completion probability, k recommended searches).
     - Baseline pane: its search list only, with no tree.

     U7 ui: answer view with citation hover

     src/lib/citations.ts:
     - Rewrite Sources lines so their indented URLs become autolinks rather than
       code.
     - A small remark plugin turns [n] inside text nodes into a citeRef node.
     - A number with no matching Citation stays plain [n].
     - Tested with vitest.

     AnswerView + CitationRef:
     - An amber scope_warning banner; streamText in a pre-wrap block until
       answer arrives, then react-markdown + remark-gfm.
     - The hover or focus card shows the evidence text, stance, confidence,
       tier, date and document title.
     - Click goes to /docs/{run}/{doc}?p={location.paragraph_index} and posts
       ui.evidence_opened.
     - The baseline renders plain markdown plus its citation URL list.

     U8 ui: evidence, claims and critic tabs

     - EvidenceTable: claim, stance, tier, date, doc and confidence, with a
       branch filter. Clicking a row opens the document view (posting
       ui.evidence_opened).
     - ClaimList: status badges with text labels. A contested claim shows its
       supporting and contradicting evidence. A flag checkbox posts
       ui.claim_flagged and feeds claim_ids_flagged.
     - CriticPanel: every CriticReport list, the recommended searches, and
       completion probability. The tab counts appear in the tab labels.

     U9 ui: usage footer and feedback

     - UsageFooter: searches, fetches, agents, rounds, seconds and tokens (as
       "41k"), preferring the record's usage once the run is terminal. It shows
       a "budget hit" chip on budget_exhausted, and the LangSmith ↗ link or
       "tracing off".
     - FeedbackControls: thumbs up/down plus a comment, and the flagged claims
       on prime. Enabled after run.finished, then locked with ✓ and "LangSmith
       ✓" or "saved locally" from the response.

     U10 ui: document view

     src/app/docs/[runId]/[docId]/page.tsx + DocumentView:
     - Header: title, tier, publisher, doc type, external id, effective/revision
       dates, URL.
     - Paragraphs are shown with their index, fetched with offset/limit 200, and
       the page is derived from ?p. ?p scrolls to that paragraph and highlights
       it.
     - A sidebar lists the document's evidence.
     - A text_error notice replaces the paragraphs when the text can't be shown.

     U11 ui: runs list and run detail with Plan tab

     - /runs: a RunsTable with question, mode, depth, status chip (including
       interrupted and example), started time and usage, linking to the detail
       page.
     - /runs/[id]: the right-pane layout fed by useRun, plus the Plan tab,
       PlanTab:
       - a branches table (id, question, rationale, source hint, priority,
         depends_on), stop criteria and budget;
       - a <pre> of planCode, or "plan code not recorded for this run".

     U12 ui: bench table

     /bench + BenchTable:
     - The configs × 05 §2 metrics grid shows mean ± spread (n); the composite
       and judge errors appear on each config.
     - Per-tier and per-domain expanders (flat values, possibly null, shown as
       "—").
     - prd_targets shown as met / unmet, with experiment links.
     - {missing: true} shows the make bench command.

     D1 docs: UI as built

     - docs/07 gets an as-built section: SSE is direct and REST goes through the
       rewrite, the types path, the absorbed contract quirks, the disabled opt
       radio, feedback enabled after finish, and the env sources.
     - README gets a UI section (start the API and pnpm dev, the env variables,
       pnpm gen:types, pnpm test).
     - Remaining docs/11 lines.

     Reuse

     - API: routes and models in prime_search/api/main.py and
       prime_search/api/models.py; OpenAPI at /openapi.json; the event and SSE
       contract in prime_search/api/sse.py.
     - Reducer reference: the event handlers in prime_search/render.py (critic
       suffix detection, both task.done shapes).
     - Answer format: prime_search/agents/synthesizer.py section headings and
       evidence/cite.py Sources lines (for citations.ts).
     - Test data: the real local runs listed below.

     Verification

     --exit-code src/types/api.ts

     Chrome gate (Claude in Chrome; the user's servers on :3000 and

          tree with 2 round separators and a critic label; Plan tab shows "not

          /docs/...?p= highlighted.
        - /runs/01a09b5b-7a6b-7603-b110-35762dba7768: contested claims and 2

        - Baseline /runs/01a09c22-b01b-7147-b297-05635f132c6a.
        - /runs/01a09ba7-638e-76d9-a2a4-7cc3a33c19ca: stuck → interrupted/failed

        - Baseline completes first while prime continues.
        - Network: an EventSource for each run to :8765, and no console errors.

     Then run /spec-review for 2.5 and stop for the gate.

      361  - 2026-09-13 — Task 2.4: the API is written up as built in 07 
           §7, 01 §2 and a README section with a curl check. `tests/test_
           api_openapi.py` requires every JSON route to have a typed 200 
           schema and the path set to match 07 §7's table, because 2.5 ge
           nerates `ui/src/types.ts` from the OpenAPI schema (07 §8) and 
           an untyped route would reach the UI as `unknown` — 07 §7–8
      362  - 2026-09-13 — Task 2.4 spec review, three stream bugs fixed. 
           (1) `emit` assigned `seq` under the write lock but published a
           fter releasing it, so two concurrent sub-agents could publish 
           seq 6 before 5; the SSE stream, deduping by high-water mark, t
           hen dropped 5 for good, and a reconnect from `Last-Event-ID: 6
           ` could not recover it. Append and publish now run under one r
           eentrant lock, subscribers keep their own lock, and subscriber
           s receive events in `seq` order, at the cost of emitters waiti
           ng on fast subscriber callbacks. (2) A reconnect carrying the 
           last event's id skipped `run.finished` and then sent the synth
           etic interrupted finish, so a browser EventSource auto-reconne
           cting to a completed run would show it failed; a `run.finished
           ` the client already has now ends the stream quietly. (3) A ru
           n not started by this process (the CLI) was called interrupted
            after any one-second gap; the stream now follows its file and
            calls it interrupted only once the file has been quiet for 18
           0 s, since a prime model call can take minutes. The mid-run SS
           E test now releases the runner only after the stream subscribe
           d, and the fake runner emits from several threads — 02 §4, 06 
           §4, 07 §9
      363  - 2026-09-13 — Task 2.4 (user decision): the API port is confi

           .0.1) in the shell or `.env`, with a default of 8765 instead o
           f 01 §2's 8000. On the user's Windows machine HTTP.sys (PID 4)
